body_text:
A deductive system is *sound* when $\Gamma\vdash\varphi$ implies
$\Gamma\models\varphi$, and *complete* when the converse holds.
Soundness says that the rules prove no semantically invalid
consequence. Completeness says that every semantic consequence
expressible in the language is, in principle, formally derivable.
